questions.q: What is MySQL Router's core role in an InnoDB Cluster?
options: The storage engine that stores InnoDB Cluster's data
A lightweight, stateless middleware that routes client connections to the correct cluster member based on current topology
The consensus protocol Group Replication uses internally
A backup tool for logical dumps
questions.explain: Router doesn't store data or participate in consensus — it proxies client connections to the correct backend based on cluster metadata.

questions.q: How is MySQL Router typically provisioned against a cluster?
options: Router configures itself automatically with no bootstrap step
By running CHANGE REPLICATION SOURCE TO on the Router host
By manually editing my.cnf on every application server
mysqlrouter --bootstrap, pointed at any member of the cluster
questions.explain: Bootstrapping reads the cluster's metadata and writes Router's configuration, so the DBA doesn't hand-track which member is primary.

questions.q: What does Router's default read-write port (6446) do?
options: Only accepts X Protocol connections
Load-balances connections across all read-only replicas
Routes every connection to whichever member is currently the cluster's primary
Blocks all write traffic for safety
questions.explain: Port 6446 is the classic-protocol read-write port, always pointed at the current primary regardless of failovers.

questions.q: What does Router's default read-only port (6447) do with multiple available replicas?
options: Routes to the primary only
Sends every connection to the same single replica
Requires the application to specify which replica by name
Load-balances (round-robin by default) connections across the available read-only members
questions.explain: The read-only port distributes read connections across available replicas rather than sending all traffic to one.

questions.q: How does statement-aware read/write splitting differ from the classic two-port model?
options: It replaces Group Replication entirely
It requires the application to open a separate connection for every single query
It inspects individual statements on a single connection and can route reads to a replica and writes to the primary automatically
It only works with the X Protocol, never the classic protocol
questions.explain: Unlike the two-port model that requires the application to choose a port up front, statement-aware splitting works within one connection, handling mixed reads and writes.
